I stand corrected for me previous review: one website that was giving me the biggest of troubles was attempting to do its own dark-mode, saw this app working: and both doubled down and looped in itself, creating weird artifacts that (Well, I think I was seeing the matrix..).
Whitelisted the site, reset the website to use its own darkmode, and everything works great again.

One point I bring back from my previous 3-star review: "this extension is my go-to plugin for every system I use Firefox on". Really, I value a good dark filter over ad-blockers.

I've used Dark Reader for YEARS but I'm finally throwing in the towel. At least on Firefox, this extension will lag your browser to death. I spent a whole week trying to trial and error what extensions were causing such huge memory usage issues and constantly causing sites to lag. I figured it was something like ublock, canvas blocker, or chrome mask. Nope. Everything lead back to Dark Reader.

This extension has helped with my eye-strain issues so much. I seriously hate to get rid of it but I can no longer look over the performance issues. Please, figure out a way to make this extension lighter or at least a stripped back version. I would love to come back and write a nicer review. For now, I will be using Stylus and simply grabbing user dark themes where I can.

Rating 5 stars because this feature is invaluable, and I've been happy to donate to the extension's development. This extension made giant strides since a few years ago; I almost don't need to disable it to unbreak sites. The performance could have been better, though.

Yes, it creates a dark-mode version of any page you visit. Sadly, it is not working correctly with more modern pages. Transparency is not considered either. 
On many pages, the overall lay-out of the page gets difficult to read. 
For example, shops that have transparent images will have a dark background everywhere, with dark text and barely visible images. 
Contact fields will mostly be dark as well, or borders disappear. 

It is sad that dark-mode is not normal yet on many websites. Sadly, this app doesn't work properly in most cases for me.
Very handy extension that saves my eyes. If something breaks, you can disable it just for a specific site, there's no need to disable the entire extension
It's great in general but doesn't detect dark mode on some websites, like outlook.cloud.microsoft.
Hate light mode on websites? Use this.

Finally, a standardized dark mode for the web. Works flawlessly out-of-the-box on 99% of websites. I've tried Chrome's dark mode flag, other extensions, etc, and this one is the best by far because it's existed for 10+ years and the community constantly maintains a dedicated list of CSS fixes for each individual website.

Short version: It's SPYWARE.

I don't know what other people are talking about, but I've noticed absolutely no performance issues even with my admittedly strange configuration. Seems to work really well and without any major issues, save for one. it tries to phone home constantly for no reason by default, and there's no obvious way to disable this "feature". Moreover, it doesn't look like other extensions are capable of blocking these connections, so a firewall is a must just for a dark mode extension that more or less just makes some CSS tweaks on the fly.

So...spyware.
